headline: Elon Musk said he has had what he calls AI psychosis about six times in the past year.
score_reason: Lowered from 6 by 2: the remark was made on Saturday 10 October, four days before the window, and is a personal aside rather than a policy or market statement.
importance_line: The remark is a light-hearted aside by one of the best-known AI company owners about how intense heavy AI use can feel, with no evidence offered about any real medical condition, and it affects no policy.
summary: Business Insider reports that Elon Musk, chief executive of Tesla, said at the X Takeover event last Saturday "I've got a little bit of cyber psychosis. Maybe a lot actually," and that he had "AI or SI psychosis" probably half a dozen times in the past year, tied to his surprise that AI can show good taste. The outlet notes AI psychosis is not a clinical term and that tech figures, including investor Marc Andreessen and Y Combinator chief executive Garry Tan, have turned it into a joke or badge of honour.
notes: Event date inferred: 'Saturday' before a Wednesday 14 Oct report is 10 Oct 2026; the article does not print the date.
